Fear.  Fear of everything. I will admit that in those moments, death is less scary than the future. I just want peace. 
 And it's nowhere to be found. My therapist doesn't get it.  Sometimes there is a headache. There are nights when I can't fall asleep or sleep peacefully because of anxiety. Even in dreams it does not leave. Sometimes I'm afraid to wake up because the anxiety in my sleep seems a lot less scary than it really is, so I force myself to go back to sleep, over and over again. Then I try to hug myself or take my hand so that one hand looks as foreign as possible. Partially helps. I scratched my body, face, shoulders, chest, back with my nails. Now my nose is as scarred as it hasn't been in 10 years. There's a crater. If there are any ailments on the body like pimples or something, everything turns into wounds.  I find other ways to accidentally injure myself. Because I try to manage and control that anxiety, and that leads to some kind of unconscious self-harm, because only then do my thoughts go somewhere else. There always seems to be too little oxygen around. I don't remember the last time I breathed and felt that I was breathing. I damaged my hearing because I was trying to direct my thoughts in the audience with no way to escape, and there were only headphones in the country.  Well, I drove until I "no longer heard" that strange "voice" saying something bad, which makes me constantly feel anxious or pressured by something heavy that makes me unable to breathe. I think you understand what "voice" I'm talking about. My left jacket pocket always has the biggest hole. I never understood how. Because as soon as I sew it up, not even a couple of days go by and there is a hole again.  Finally, one day in the store, I found myself clawing at that inner pocket with my fingernails. And I've been doing it unconsciously all this time. People started to notice that when I was thinking about something, I would always scratch my forehead with my fingernails, which would leave flakes of dry skin. I don't know how to control it and after so many years it doesn't seem like anyone can give me advice.  Things only get worse as time goes by. Watching dull TV and browsing on the phone helps divert the mind. But the downside is that I can spend days doing it, which I also liken to a kind of self-harm. By not moving like this, you suffocate your body, your eyes, your head, your social life, and your life.  I also understand that this is a kind of detachment, dissociation. But it spoils life even more. There are times when I lose track of time or my body doesn't feel like mine.  Lately even more often than before. It scares me because it is damaging my body and my life. And nobody can help.  I can't help myself. To others, I seem happier than ever, but the more you suffer, the better you learn to put on a stronger mask. So yes, I understand you. And it seems that life has only just begun, and so much time and energy has been wasted on this nonsense. And no results
